 The bridge was struck shortly after 1 p.m., officials said. The cause of the accident was under investigation.
 The Tacony-Palmyra Bridge after a cargo ship struck the bridge Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, in Philadelphia. Read more Elizabeth Robertson / Staff Photographer by Robert Moran and Lacey Latch Updated  Nov. 12, 2026, 9:14 p.m. ET | Published  Nov. 12, 2026, 4:35 p.m. ET Listen to article •   0:00 min The Tacony-Palmyra Bridge on Thursday night reopened to vehicle and pedestrian traffic after it sustained minor damage when it was hit earlier by a passing ship, officials said.
 David Levinsky, spokesperson for Burlington County , said that repairs were still underway, but two lanes — one in each direction — were reopened around 8:40 p.m.
 Earlier on Thursday, the county posted a Facebook update saying the bridge was closed to all vehicular and pedestrian traffic “due to an investigation into a potential collision involving a ship passing beneath the drawbridge.”
 The county said the strike occurred shortly after 1 p.m. during a bridge opening for marine traffic.
 No injuries were reported.
 The Burlington County Bridge Commission, which runs the bridge, was investigating the extent of the damage on the bridge and the cause of the accident, the county said.
 Word first spread on social media about the ship hitting the bridge when State Rep. Ed Neilson, of Northeast Philly, alerted followers on Facebook .
 “The bridge is unable to close at this time causing a disruption to traffic between Philadelphia and New Jersey,” Neilson said.
